heuristic.applicability: Prefer when switching into the skill at an intermediate represented state, when red and blue approach poses could otherwise be confused, or when preserving local IK continuity from the current arm configuration is important. The high-level agent must choose phase from observable relations: drawer-front retreat before red contact; red grasp/transport/place while red is being approached/held; red release-to-blue after pad support and opening; blue pickup when TCP is near blue and closure/lift is intended.

handoff.entry_conditions: Drawer_position is above 0.26 m and phase is selected from current observable state. History remains two causal frames across a policy switch; only episode-start history may be duplicated.
handoff.exit_conditions: Terminate after red pad placement/release and, for the intended overlap, once blue is centered, fingers are closed, and blue/TCP co-motion indicates initial lift. Phase alone is not a grasp certificate.
handoff.failure_signatures: Caller phase disagrees with geometry, gripper closes on the wrong object, red lacks co-motion, red is off-pad or follows retreat, TCP revisits red after release, blue is not under TCP at closure, or IK reports an unreachable local target.
handoff.overlap_role: All actions in [230,470) and [600,850) remain covered. Coarse phase boundaries retain release actions on both sides of the successor overlap and include blue approach/contact/lift.
handoff.successor_readiness: blue_insert is callable from 600 with predecessor-release context. For this prior use red_release_to_blue through transit, then blue_pickup near the observed blue approach; clean successor readiness is established blue lift.

heuristic.limitations: A wrong phase argument can deliberately select the wrong object or gripper mode. Coarse boundaries include within-phase approach and contact variation, and local coordinates are not by construction invariant to a large red or goal displacement. Rotation-vector transfer assumes relative rotations remain away from the pi branch. Use the red-object prior for displaced red pickup and the destination-centered prior for moved-pad placement; none of the set proves grasp recovery, collision avoidance, or unreachable-state recovery.
heuristic.pipeline_implications: Train one independent unchanged DiffusionBackbone with a phase one-hot concatenated to two causal relational frames. Bind four contiguous ranges per demonstration—[230,445), [445,620), [620,780), [780,850)—so every assigned action and both overlaps remain supervised while phase semantics are explicit. Labels are 7-D chunk-TCP-relative translation, relative rotation vector, and gripper. decode_action composes with the causal chunk TCP, then uses fresh-joint IK. No recurrent phase memory or future state enters inference, and diffusion loss is the sole objective.
heuristic.rationale: Observed: both inspected demonstrations start with a closed gripper at the drawer front, open by 240, move through a long retreat/approach before red closure around 445, lift by 470, descend near 600, then release timing differs (demo1000 is opening by 608 while demo1001 remains closed at 610). Both then retreat/transit and approach blue, but their blue contact/lift timing and terminal height differ. These repeated geometric states with different intended objects create phase ambiguity, and adjacent skills may switch into any represented overlap state. Expected benefit: a coarse caller phase plus TCP-relative local targets conditions the mode explicitly and replans corrections from the actual intermediate TCP/configuration. It does not demonstrate recovery from unseen contact errors.
heuristic.statement: Phase-conditioned local Cartesian correction. Learn each target relative to the TCP pose at chunk construction: translation in that TCP frame, relative rotation vector, and gripper scalar. A required semantic phase argument selects one of four coarse responsibilities, while relational causal inputs and measured robot state retain geometry and reachability. This targets entry states produced at different points by adjacent skills and phase aliasing between red approach, red transport, post-release blue transit, and blue pickup.

subgoal: Primary responsibility: after the drawer is open, acquire the exposed red block, lift and carry it to the marked outside pad, lower it, release it, and retreat. The segment then intentionally continues through the approach, contact, grasp, and initial lift of the blue block for the next handoff. Observed contact/motion: the red block is pinched with fingers near 0.018 m, carried at roughly 0.30 m height, lowered to the pad, released as the fingers open, and left at z about 0.020 m; the TCP retreats before crossing to blue. Entry observation 230 has drawer_position 0.300, TCP still at the drawer front, and fingers near 0.007 m, so the skill is supervised to release/retract before acquiring red. At exit observation 850, red is already on the pad and blue is gripped with fingers near 0.018 m and lifted to z about 0.061-0.193 m, depending on occurrence. Examples: demo1000 indices 470/560/600/610 show red lift, carry, pad descent, and release; 700/800/850 show retreat, blue approach, and blue lift. Images at demo1000 indices 560, 610, 800, and 850 support the pad and blue-pickup interpretation. Purpose/expected benefit: this isolates red placement while retaining both adjacent transitions; overlap is expected to reduce sensitivity to switching before red grasp or before blue grasp, but it does not demonstrate recovery from an off-pad release.
